newsitem.title: UK: UTGC aims to undercut European telecoms firms.
newsitem.headline: UTGC aims to undercut European telecoms firms.

text.p: Telecoms company UTG Communications (UTGC) officially launched operations on Wednesday and vowed to offer European business customers substantial discounts against local domestic telephone firms.
The company, listed in the U.S. on NASDAQ last month, aims to profit from the opening up of the European telecoms market to full competition from 1998.

Chairman Tom Combrinck, who owns some 63 percent of the company, told a press conference that UTGC planned to undercut domestic 'phone companies by 20-40 percent in the European business international direct dial market.
UTGC's services are being tailored for small and medium-sized corporate customers. It aims to focus its activity on France, Germany, Belgium and Luxembourg, Switzerland, Hungary and Austria.
The company is headquartered in New Jersey, U.S. and based its European operations in the Swiss town of Zug, with a support and marketing hub in London.
Hoewever, it has no immediate plans to enter the British or American market where competition is fierce.
UTGC also said it could undercut the international roaming agreements of existing European mobile 'phone operators by up to 50 percent.

It said its service was based on a fibre-optic network leased from Telecom Italia. It also owns its own "switches' which allow the company to route its international traffic by the most economical routes at any time.
UTGC said it expected revenue to grow from around $36 million this year to $150 million in its third year of operation.
It is ultimately aiming for a 1-2 percent share of the European market -- annual revenues of $2 billion.
